data.narrative:
Mujin is a Series C robotics and manufacturing automation company that has raised $85M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine private companies and one public peer (277810.KQ) operating in the same sector and stage vicinity, including Exotec, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Hadrian.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, using total raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $144M. The peer-median approach benchmarks against seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.6B and a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. This method reflects the wider distribution of late-stage robotics valuations in the current market.

Synthesizing both approaches produces a triangulated range of $123M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $897M. The wide spread reflects fundamental uncertainty regarding Mujin's commercialization trajectory and near-term unit economics relative to peers. The stage-progression method suggests downside valuation anchored to capital deployed; the peer set suggests substantial upside if Mujin demonstrates comparable traction to Series B/D stage robotics companies. Key drivers of final valuation within this range will be revenue growth, customer concentration, deployment scale, and gross margins relative to the peer cohort.
